Let
\[
B(x,y)=x_1y_3+x_2y_4-x_3y_1-x_4y_2\in R.
\]
Then \(\omega(x,y)=[t^{m-1}]B(x,y)\).

Because \(L\) is \(N\)-stable, it is an \(R\)-submodule of \(V\). Also, \(N|_L\) having two Jordan blocks of size \(m\) means
\[
L\simeq R^2
\]
as an \(R\)-module. Finally, \(\omega|_{L\times L}=0\) is equivalent to \(B|_{L\times L}=0\): indeed, for \(x,y\in L\),
\[
0=\omega(t^k x,y)=[t^{m-1}]\,t^kB(x,y)
\]
for every \(0\le k\le m-1\), so every coefficient of \(B(x,y)\) is zero.

Thus admissible subspaces are exactly rank \(2\) free \(R\)-Lagrangian submodules of the symplectic \(R\)-module \(R^4\).

First count admissible \(L\). A primitive vector in \(R^4\) is one not lying in \(tR^4\), so the number of primitive vectors is
\[
q^{4m}-q^{4m-4}=q^{4m-4}(q^4-1).
\]
Each rank \(1\) free summand has
\[
|R^\times|=q^m-q^{m-1}=q^{m-1}(q-1)
\]
primitive generators, so the number of rank \(1\) free summands is
\[
q^{3m-3}\frac{q^4-1}{q-1}
=q^{3m-3}(q+1)(q^2+1).
\]
For a fixed isotropic line \(\ell\), Lagrangians containing \(\ell\) correspond to rank \(1\) free summands of a rank \(2\) symplectic quotient, so there are \(|\mathbb P^1(R)|=q^{m-1}(q+1)\) of them. Each Lagrangian \(R^2\) contains the same number \(q^{m-1}(q+1)\) of lines, hence these factors cancel. Therefore
\[
\#\{L\}=q^{3m-3}(q+1)(q^2+1).
\]

Fix one admissible \(L_1\). The admissible \(L_2\) transverse to it are Lagrangian complements. After choosing one complement, every such \(L_2\) is the graph of a symmetric \(2\times2\) matrix over \(R\), so there are
\[
|R|^3=q^{3m}
\]
choices.

Now fix a transverse pair \(L_1,L_2\). Any \(L_3\) transverse to \(L_1\) is the graph of a symmetric map \(S:L_2\to L_1\). It is also transverse to \(L_2\) exactly when \(S\) is invertible. Thus we need the number of invertible symmetric \(2\times2\) matrices over \(R\).

Such a matrix has form
\[
\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ b&c\end{pmatrix},
\]
and is invertible iff \(ac-b^2\in R^\times\), which depends only on reduction mod \(t\). Over \(\mathbb F_q\), the singular triples satisfy \(ac=b^2\). If \(a\ne0\), then \(c=b^2/a\), giving \(q(q-1)\) triples; if \(a=0\), then \(b=0\), giving \(q\) triples. Thus there are \(q^2\) singular triples and
\[
q^3-q^2=q^2(q-1)
\]
invertible symmetric matrices over \(\mathbb F_q\). Each lifts in \(q^{3(m-1)}\) ways, so the number over \(R\) is
\[
q^{3(m-1)}q^2(q-1).
\]

Therefore the number of ordered pairwise transverse triples is
\[
q^{3m-3}(q+1)(q^2+1)\cdot q^{3m}\cdot q^{3m-3}q^2(q-1)
=
q^{9m-4}(q^4-1).
\]

\[
\boxed{q^{9m-4}(q^4-1)}
\]
